notes: RUBRIC read off this workbook's own header row (Results!H1:Z1), not assumed: Pool play Win 3 / Tie 1 / Loss 0, plus two 1/0 flag bonuses - 'Top Table' (finished first in group) 5 and 'Knockouts' (advanced to the Round of 32) 5. Knockouts pay per round on a Win / Shootout Loss pair: R32 10/2, R16 20/4, QF 50/10, SF 100/20, Final 200/40. Pot bonus 48 (Results!Z1). 48-team, 12-group, Round-of-32 format.

A SHOOTOUT LOSS IS ITS OWN OUTCOME TYPE, not a win and not a draw. It appears only in the knockout columns and is scored at 20% of that round's win value. Germany (R32 shootout loss) and Netherlands (R32 shootout loss) and Colombia (R16 shootout loss) are the three teams that used it. Germany: 2W 0T 1L + TT + KO + R32 shootout loss = 6+0+5+5+2 = 18, matching the workbook.

POT BONUS IS NOT TRANSCRIBED AS AN EVENT, per instruction: it is expressed only as rules[] {kind: group_rank_bonus, group_attr: 'pot', rate: 48} so the engine must derive it. The workbook's FINAL total (Results!AC, 'Total', which INCLUDES the bonus) is what lands in expected.points. The pre-bonus figure lives only in the workbook's 'Pre-Bonus Tally' column and is not carried in this JSON; the engine should reproduce it from events alone.

The pot-bonus tie in pot 4 is a genuine four-way tie at 9 pre-bonus points: Bosnia-Herzegovina, Sweden, Congo DR and Ghana all went 1W-1T-1L (5 pts) and all advanced (+5 knockouts, no Top Table), = 9, and all four exited the R32 in regulation. 48 / 4 = 12 each. Cape Verde is the near-miss at 8 (0W-3T-0L + knockouts).

OWNER IDENTITY: this workbook writes FULL NAMES in every owner cell ('Ezra Pemstein', 'Craig Thompson', 'Ed Zhang', 'Zachary Long', 'Joey Anthony', 'Samuel Rosen'), unlike the sibling pools which use first names or initials. owners[].label and owners[].name are both the full name. The trade Detail strings, by contrast, use first names ('Zach buys...', 'Sam short sells...'); the paired 'New Owner' column gives the full name, so the mapping Zach->Zachary Long, Sam->Samuel Rosen, Craig->Craig Thompson, Joey->Joey Anthony, Ed->Ed Zhang, Ezra->Ezra Pemstein is established by the workbook itself, not inferred.

CONSORTIA: the Auction Pro tab carries a 'Consortia Leaders' / 'Additional Members' pair of columns. Each of the 6 bidding entities is a consortium of 1-2 people; only the leader ever appears as an owner of a lot, so the consortium members are NOT owners in entries[]. Recorded under the top-level 'consortia' key. Samuel Rosen has no additional member (members: []). The additional members (Zack Miller, Damon Hatheway, Shaun McGuire, Greg Karabinos, Kurt Dehut) appear nowhere else in the workbook except that Shaun McGuire also shows up as a zero-dollar player row on the leftover NFL tab.

The 'Funds Flow' block on the Auction Pro tab settles at the consortium level and names payees as consortium pairs: Ezra pays 7,650.672952 to Craig (and a 3,825.336476 figure sits one column further right, i.e. the per-head half); Ed pays 4,385.760728 to Craig and 23.4609883 'To Joey / Kurt'; Zach pays 9,714.379064 to Sam and 874.130039 'To Joey / Kurt'. This is the only place the workbook treats a consortium as a single settlement counterparty.

TRADES ARE TRANSCRIBED ONE OBJECT PER LEG (26 objects for 13 economic trades), because both legs carry their own date, % of Asset, Value of Traded Asset and Net Trade Value in the workbook and short/synthetic legs are only identifiable from the leg text. Both legs of a trade share the same sheet_ref (the workbook's Trade ID) and the same from/to, so a loader can collapse them by sheet_ref. 'cash' is that leg's Net Trade Value; 'asset_value' is its Value of Traded Asset; 'leg_side' is one of buy / sell / synthetic_buy / short_sell; 'leg_owner' is the workbook's 'New Owner' cell for that leg.

SHORT SALES AND SYNTHETIC BUYS: 8 of the 13 trades are synthetic pairs (a 'synthetic buys' leg against a 'short sells' leg) rather than real transfers of the lot - France 50% (Joey synthetic long / Sam short), Egypt 50% (Ed long / Sam short), Uruguay 50% twice (Sam long / Craig short on 6/11, then Sam long AGAIN / Joey short on 6/15 - Sam doubled the same synthetic position), Sweden 50% (Craig long / Sam short), Czechia 50% (Craig long / Sam short), Belgium 50% @ $3,500 (Craig long / Sam short). Sam is the short seller on 5 of them. Only 5 trades are real ownership transfers: Haiti 100% @ $200, Saudi Arabia 50% @ $740, Spain 50% @ $9,000, Norway 10% @ $5,000, Paraguay 50% @ $1,433, Spain 10% @ $13,900 (that is 6 real legs across trades 1,2,3,12,13,14).

IMPORTANT: entries[].owners records the AUCTION ownership as the workbook's own Owner #1 / Owner #2 columns state it, and the workbook does NOT restate ownership after trades. Spain is still listed as Craig Thompson 100% even though Craig sold 50% to Sam (trade 3) and 10% to Zach (trade 14); Haiti is still Samuel Rosen even though Zach bought it outright (trade 1). The trade economics are carried entirely by the separate 'Trade Impact' column, which the 26 trade legs reproduce exactly. Do not net the trades into the shares - that would double-count.

Trade ID 11 exists in the workbook as two rows with the text 'Intentionally left blank - Scotland trade off BS' and no numbers. It is NOT transcribed as a trade. Trade IDs 15-18 are pre-numbered empty placeholder row pairs. So 14 IDs, 13 real trades, 26 legs.

MTM / VALUATION TAB ('Market Odds'): this is the World Cup analogue of the NFL pools' Kalshi week-zero model. Layout: one row per team, keyed Group / Pot / Team, then a Pts column (current earned pre-bonus points), then eight PROBABILITY columns - 'To Advance', 'To Win Group', 'To Win R32', 'To Win R16', 'To Win Quarterfinals', 'To Win Semis', 'To Win Finals', 'Pool Bonus' - then Pts (expected total), FV (fair value in dollars) and MTM (FV minus cost). Row 1 above the probability columns holds the point value each probability is multiplied by: 1 (per pool-play point already banked), 5 (To Advance = the Knockouts flag), 5 (To Win Group = Top Table), 10 / 20 / 50 / 100 / 200 (the five knockout round wins), and 48 (Pool Bonus), with 1538 (total pool points) sitting at the end. So the inputs it needs are: (a) per-team market-implied probabilities for advancing out of the group, winning the group, and winning each of the five knockout rounds, (b) a per-team probability of taking its pot bonus, (c) each team's already-banked points, and (d) the pool-wide total-points denominator and $/point. FV = expected points x $ per point. In the exported snapshot all eight probability cells are EMPTY and only the realised flags remain (Pool Bonus = 1.0 for Spain / Switzerland / Norway and 0.25 for each of the four tied pot-4 teams), because the workbook was last saved after the tournament resolved - so the tab shows structure, not live odds. The 48-shootout-loss outcomes are NOT modelled here: the probability grid has no shootout-loss column, so its expected points are systematically a little low for teams that can exit on penalties.

It also carries its OWN Secondary Trades block of 15 NFL trades dated 8/13-8/14/25 (Lion King crossbook, synthetic longs/shorts on the Pats, Dolphins, Raiders, Texans, plus % transfers of the Ravens, Commanders, Chiefs, Texans, Packers, Jets, Eagles) whose text survived but whose every dollar value is #REF!. Ignored entirely, per contract. (2) 'Sheet1' holds a live-looking NFL auction: 32 NFL teams with Bid / Owner / Owner #2 (first names) and a trailing note 'Sam / Zach: 25% Crossbook of everything touched'. (3) 'Scoring Rubric' holds the NFL scoring rubric (old and new: per-win 20, playoff berth 25, div 50, conf 100, SB berth 200, win SB 500, per point-differential-above--100 pool 100, 11420 denominator, 2x primetime point-differential multiplier) plus a fully populated NFL results grid. (4) 'Valuations Over Time' is an NFL week-by-week MTM history (Draft, Week 0-18) naming NFL owners including Joshua Melnick, Ian Culnane and Shaun McGuire who never appear in the World Cup pool. These four tabs together look like the NFL edition's workbook, saved-as and partially overwritten.

expected.realized_return is the workbook's ENTRY-level 'Realized Payoff' (Results!AD), not the per-owner 'Split Payoff' (Results!AE). For the 8 two-owner lots Split Payoff is exactly half of Realized Payoff - Portugal is the example called out in the brief: Realized Payoff $1,455.526658, Split Payoff $727.763329, split Joey Anthony / Ezra Pemstein. The workbook also carries 'Est. Fully Loaded Payoff Per Owner' (Results!AG) and 'Est. MTM' (Results!AH) columns which are not transcribed.

Two lots tie at $730 (Saudi Arabia, Congo DR) and two at $1,700 (Sweden, Bosnia-Herzegovina); lot_order comes from the Auction Pro 'Order' column (1-48, complete with no gaps or duplicates) and disambiguates them. Spain was lot 1 and went for $8,100; France was the most expensive lot at $9,090.

Team names are transcribed with the workbook's own diacritics and spellings: 'Turkiye' is written Türkiye, 'Curacao' is written Curaçao, and the workbook uses 'Congo DR', 'Ivory Coast', 'Czechia', 'Cape Verde', 'United States', 'South Korea', 'Bosnia-Herzegovina'.
Six teams finished with 0 points (Tunisia, Uzbekistan, Panama, Haiti, Iraq, Jordan - all 0W-0T-3L) and therefore $0 realized payoff, a total write-off of $2,970 of entry cost.

No bundles and no placeholders in this pool: all 48 lots are single named national teams, one lot per team, so entries[].kind is 'single' throughout and teams[] always has exactly one member. teams[].seed is null (a World Cup has pots, not seeds); the pot is carried in attributes.pot and is the group_attr the pot bonus keys on.
